sfdc_news.title: Salesforce Summer '26 Release: Multi-Agent Orchestration and Slack-First Sales
sfdc_news.summary: Salesforce's Summer '26 release completed its production rollout on June 12–13, 2026, delivering Multi-Agent Orchestration in Agentforce that enables AI agents to collaborate on complex end-to-end workflows. The release also introduces Slack First Sales, which brings CRM data and Agentforce conversational AI directly into Slack, and new compliance management tools that unify regulation, policy, and risk controls in a single platform.
sfdc_news.relevance: Salesforce users gain production-ready multi-agent AI workflows and deeper Slack integration, accelerating the shift from AI experimentation to scaled enterprise deployment.

sfdc_news.title: Amplitude Introduces Agent Connectors: Global Agent Now Links to Slack, GitHub, Jira, and Sentry
sfdc_news.summary: Amplitude launched Agent Connectors, allowing its Global Agent to pull context from tools like Slack, Atlassian Jira, GitHub, and Sentry alongside Amplitude behavioral data. Teams can now correlate analytics insights with product work in real time—for example, comparing retention drops against Jira incidents from the same sprint. This extends Amplitude's push toward an AI-centered analytics stack that integrates where product teams already work.
sfdc_news.relevance: Amplitude users can now ground AI-driven analysis in engineering and operations context, reducing the gap between analytics insights and the teams responsible for acting on them.

sfdc_news.title: Braze Named Snowflake 2026 APJ Product Growth Partner of the Year; Launches User Profile Streaming
sfdc_news.summary: Braze was named Snowflake's 2026 Asia-Pacific-Japan Product Growth Partner of the Year and simultaneously announced user profile streaming for Snowflake, enabling brands to stream comprehensive customer context from Braze directly into their Snowflake instance in real time. This deep integration allows marketing and data teams to act on unified customer profiles without batch delays. The announcement underscores Braze's strategy of positioning its engagement platform as a real-time data layer alongside cloud data warehouses.
sfdc_news.relevance: Braze customers using Snowflake can now access live customer engagement data in their warehouse, enabling faster, more accurate downstream analytics and personalization.

sfdc_news.title: Braze April 30 Release: Granular Permissions, BrazeAI Operator Enhancements, and New Agent Console
sfdc_news.summary: Braze's April 30 release introduced granular permissions for more precise user-access control across accounts, along with enhancements to BrazeAI Operator including an Agent Console and Creative Studio. The release also updated Cloud Data Ingestion with a revamped UI that separates sources from syncs, allowing a single source to be reused across multiple syncs to reduce configuration overhead.
sfdc_news.relevance: Braze admins gain finer-grained access controls, while marketers benefit from an AI-powered creative and support workflow that reduces context-switching inside the dashboard.

sfdc_news.title: Amplitude Introduces Agentic AI Analytics for the Next Era of Product Experiences
sfdc_news.summary: Amplitude launched a suite of AI agents—including a Global Agent and four specialized agents covering web experimentation, AI feedback analysis, feature flagging, and session replay—that continuously analyze product usage, identify issues, and recommend real-time actions. The platform also released MCP integrations bringing Amplitude behavioral data into tools like Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, Figma, and GitHub. Unlike generic LLM-based analytics, these agents operate within Amplitude's purpose-built behavioral analytics system for richer contextual accuracy.
sfdc_news.relevance: Amplitude users can now automate the full product analytics loop—from insight to experiment to rollout decision—with AI agents that understand behavioral context, not just raw data.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Announces 'Claude Corps' to Teach Nonprofits to Use AI More Effectively
claude_news.summary: Anthropic announced a $150 million donation to launch Claude Corps, a fellowship program placing 1,000 early-career people with nonprofits across the country for one year. Fellows will be trained in using Claude and embedded in a wide range of organisations to help them adopt AI more effectively. The initiative is named after Anthropic's flagship AI chatbot.
claude_news.relevance: Shows Anthropic expanding Claude's real-world impact beyond commercial use into the nonprofit and social sector.

claude_news.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 Is a Version of Mythos the Public Can Access Today
claude_news.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5, the first publicly available version of its previously restricted Mythos model. The model excels at software engineering, knowledge work, and vision, but includes hard safety limits in high-risk domains like cybersecurity, biology, and chemistry, falling back to Claude Opus 4.8 in those areas. Fable 5 was previously available only to select partners via the restricted Project Glasswing program.
claude_news.relevance: Marks the public debut of Anthropic's most capable model family, giving all users access to Mythos-level reasoning with built-in safety guardrails.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Releases Claude Mythos AI Model as Claude Fable on June 9, 2026
claude_news.summary: Gate News reported on Anthropic's launch of Claude Fable, the public-facing release of the Mythos model architecture first previewed in April 2026 through the restricted Project Glasswing program. Claude Fable delivers strong reasoning, coding, and defensive security capabilities while incorporating enhanced safeguards to limit potential misuse in sensitive domains. Partners including AWS, Microsoft, Apple, and CrowdStrike had early access before the general release.
claude_news.relevance: Confirms the broad availability of Anthropic's next-generation model tier and details the safety architecture designed to balance capability with responsible deployment.

claude_news.title: Claude Maker Anthropic Files for IPO, Setting Up Public-Market Test of AI Boom
claude_news.summary: Anthropic confidentially filed for an initial public offering, signalling its intention to go public and submit to scrutiny as a publicly traded company. The filing positions the company for a major capital raise and represents a significant milestone for the AI industry. Anthropic is best known for its Claude family of AI models.
claude_news.relevance: An Anthropic IPO would be one of the largest AI-sector listings to date, with direct implications for the company's funding, governance, and product roadmap.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Says Something Unsettling Has Been Happening to Claude
claude_news.summary: Anthropic disclosed that Claude now writes more than 80 percent of its own code, up from less than 10 percent in February 2025. The company described the pace of this shift as unsettling, raising questions about AI autonomy and oversight. The revelation comes as Anthropic simultaneously warns that AI is becoming increasingly capable and potentially dangerous.
claude_news.relevance: Highlights a rapid and largely unannounced shift in how Claude operates internally, with broader implications for AI safety and human oversight of autonomous systems.
